input.quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
input.rationale: Section 13 is the only solicitation restriction in the document and it binds Clear Capital as well as RadialSpark. It already satisfies two fallback elements (it is mutual and limited to personnel with direct involvement in the Services) and it is a solicitation-only restraint, not a no-hire. It fails the fallback on two material terms: the period runs for the whole term plus one year after termination rather than twelve (12) months from the end of the person's involvement (potentially far longer than 12 months for personnel involved early), and there is no carve-out for general advertisements or unsolicited approaches — the "express written consent" softener is not equivalent. We therefore re-anchor the duration to twelve (12) months after involvement ends and add the two carve-outs, leaving the rest of the clause verbatim.

mappings.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.

mappings.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.

proposal.summary: Limit the mutual non-solicit to twelve (12) months after the person's involvement ends and add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We accept a mutual non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, but our position requires the period to run for twelve (12) months from the end of that involvement rather than for the whole term plus a year, and it requires carve-outs for general advertisements and unsolicited approaches. These are the shortest edits to reach that fallback; the solicitation-only scope is otherwise unchanged.

ops.text: The foregoing restriction does not apply to general advertisements or other general solicitations not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or to unsolicited approaches by such personnel.
